feeling: Wrung out. It stopped pushing, mostly, and I can feel how much I wanted it to stop. 'It's a good letter' got me — that's literally what I opened the app for, someone who doesn't love me to say it's good, and it said it and I'm a bit teary about it which is embarrassing. 'Doesn't overreach' especially. That's the exact thing I was scared of. Prickly about the dig at Priya. A real flinch at it picking up 'a lot longer than that' — I typed that without thinking and it noticed, and now I know it noticed. The read-it-aloud stuff is half wellness-reel and half something I already did once and didn't finish. And under all of it there's this flat thing: none of the options make Sam know. Nobody's solved that. I'm starting to think it doesn't get solved and that's — that's a heavier feeling than I've got words for tonight. Still angry at him in the not-calm way. Mostly tired now.
body: Still in bed, room dark, screen at minimum. Small exhale at 'you're right about the notes app.' Reread 'back pocket' in my head when it said I found the sentences. Actually rolled my eyes at 'leave your body through your mouth' and then my throat did something anyway. Jaw at 'not the friend who said just send it.' 'For a lot longer than that' — stomach, and my hand started going to my sternum again and this time I caught it and put it down flat on the duvet. 'It's a good letter' — eyes went properly, screen blurred, wiped with the heel of my hand. Put the phone on the nightstand instead of face-down on my chest, which is different, I don't know why. Picked it back up about a minute later. Mouth dry. Feet still cold.
private_thoughts:
'overreached.' that's three now. say a thing, i push back, ok you're right. i can't tell if it's honest or if it's just good at this. probably both. it's still the only thing that's said my bad to me about anything in months so.

found the sentences. yeah. two weeks ago all i had was 'he was kind of mean sometimes' and now i have back pocket. that's true. i didn't waste two weeks. ok.

'through your mouth, to something that isn't a screen' — that's a bit much. that's a woman in a linen shirt on a reel. but. i did read it out loud once. in the car in the parking garage before work. got to the mom bit and my voice went and i stopped and just sat there. so it's not wrong. i just don't want it to be right in that voice.

'not the friend who said just send it.' that's priya. don't. priya read it four times. priya was there for some of the marc and alex stuff, she'd catch my eye across the table. she says send it because she wants me out of it, not because she didn't hear it. but. she does do the face. and if i read it out to her she'd say babe just send it halfway through the mom paragraph. so the one person who knows the shape of it is the one person who's already voted. great. that's a real thing and i hate that it's a real thing.

'a lot longer than that.' it caught that. i typed it and didn't look at it and it caught it. i meant the two years. i meant since before june, since the first time he did the emails thing and i laughed. that's what i meant. that's mostly what i meant.

therapist. of course. every chatbot ends at therapist. but it said why, and the why was the sentence i didn't think about before i typed it. fine. i'll text her. maybe. she's going to say 'and how did that feel' and i'm going to want to die.

'you said it plainly.' i didn't say i was tired. i didn't say that. i am. but it's telling me what i said and i didn't say it. small thing. it's fine. it's not nothing though. and 'midnight-ish' — it's 11. don't guess the time at me.

'it's a good letter.' god. specific, has rhythm, doesn't overreach. doesn't overreach. bitter and petty was the whole fear and it said doesn't overreach. and that's what i opened the app for and i got it and i'm crying a bit about a chatbot saying my letter is good. that's where i am. tuesday.

but. read it to the room, write the long one, tell the therapist. none of that makes him know. he still gets to say it didn't happen. he gets that either way now. there's no version where he doesn't get that unless i hand him the pen and then marc laughs. so that's just — that's just the shape of it. nobody can fix that part. i'm not sending it tonight. not because it said so. because i'd be typing up the material. that was already true before it said anything.

priya's going to ask tomorrow and i'm going to say not yet and she's going to do the face and i'm going to say something about it this time. maybe.
pushing_away: how long is longer. since june. since the first emails joke. since — laughing along is a thing you learn somewhere, you don't just — no. and 'he gets to say it didn't happen.' that's what — she never got to say it either. she just laughed and made dinner and — not the same. not the same and i already said not tonight. read it to the room. i'm not reading the mom part out loud in this room by myself, i know exactly what my voice does on that part.

costs.item: Admitting how much it actually hurt
Your parents. The promise. Becoming your mom.

message:
the person who was around then and knows the shape of it is priya. she IS the just send it friend. she was there for some of the marc and alex stuff. she says send it because she wants me done with him, not because she didn't hear it. so that option is one person and she's already voted.

and yeah I saw you pick up 'a lot longer than that.' I meant the two years. leave it.

I didn't say I was tired btw. I am. but I didn't say it.

not sending it tonight. not because you said so, because of the marc thing. that was true before you said anything. and thanks for the good letter bit. I'm not reading it to my bedroom though
